author: Chippewa Valley Times
title: Third-generation student prepares for automation career after graduating from CVTC
text:
Ashley DeMuth, CEO | Menomonie Area Chamber of Commerce
Ashley DeMuth, CEO | Menomonie Area Chamber of Commerce
For Thomas Sabelko, a 21-year-old from Eau Claire, the path to a career in automation began with a desire to understand how things work. Raised in a homeschooling environment, Sabelko developed skills in self-directed learning through hands-on projects and field trips.
“It was different, but it taught me how to find answers for myself,” he said. “That skill has helped me a lot.”
Sabelko enrolled in Chippewa Valley Technical College’s (CVTC) Automation Engineering Technology program, attracted by its practical approach.
“CVTC is all hands-on,” he said. “You learn it, then you apply it right away. That’s how I learn best. You learn from doing. That’s my favorite part.”
His decision to attend CVTC was influenced by family ties: his father is an alumnus who now serves on the program’s advisory board and works as an Electrical and Instrumentation supervisor at Cascades Tissue Group, a local manufacturer where both Sabelko's great-uncle and grandfather also worked.
“My great-uncle and grandpa both worked at Cascades, too. So now I’ll be the third generation,” he said.
After graduating this December, Sabelko will join Cascades Tissue Group in January—a job opportunity that arose after meeting company representatives at a career fair.
“I gave out about 10 copies of my resume,” Sabelko said. “Cascades called me back, and it just went from there. They respected that I wanted to finish school before starting, so I’ll begin in January.”
Before choosing automation as his focus area, Sabelko explored several programs at CVTC open houses.
“I thought it would be too much computer work,” Sabelko admitted. “But once I got into it, I realized it’s still really hands-on. The programming actually helps you with the hands-on work, like troubleshooting and fixing equipment. It all connects.”
Mark Husby, one of his instructors at CVTC, noted the transformation students undergo during their studies.
“I enjoy seeing those lightbulbs turn on … seeing somebody like Tom (Sabelko) come from first semester not knowing much about the subject, and just building that knowledge up to graduation,” Husby said. “We get really good students in our program. They just blend really well. They all work together, and it’s really exciting to see when they all graduate.”
Affordability was another key factor for Sabelko; he highlighted that his entire program cost around $10,000 while providing strong job prospects upon graduation.
“My whole program costs around $10,000, and I’ll graduate with a great job lined up,” he said. “It just makes sense. It’s practical, and you can start your career right away.”
Looking ahead to his new role at Cascades Tissue Group alongside his father—and following two previous generations—Sabelko expressed enthusiasm for ongoing learning in automation technology.
“I’m excited,” he said. “It’s going to be hard work, but I’m willing to learn. Automation is for people who never want to stop learning, and who love the feeling you get when you figure something out.”
